boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of California-Los Angeles, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A daylight-to-evening orientation loop through UCLA’s core landmarks, learning spaces, art, garden paths, and recreation areas.

cards.title: Start at The Bruin
cards.subtitle: Bruin Plaza · campus orientation stop
cards.notes: Meet at the bronze Bruin across from John Wooden Center, then use Bruin Plaza to orient yourself before walking campus.
cards.short_summary: Begin at UCLA’s iconic bronze mascot in the campus core.
cards.evidence_claim: UCLA identifies The Bruin as an iconic bronze statue in the heart of campus, across from John Wooden Center.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus landmark; follow current campus visitor and access guidance.

cards.title: Walk the campus spine
cards.subtitle: Bruin Walk · pedestrian route by Ackerman Union
cards.notes: Continue along the major east-west pedestrian route and pause to notice student-group tables, services, and nearby campus landmarks.
cards.short_summary: Use UCLA’s main pedestrian corridor to connect the core stops.
cards.evidence_claim: UCLA’s self-guided tour calls Bruin Walk the major east-west pedestrian route and places Ackerman Union along it.
cards.source_title: UCLA Self-Guided Walking Tour of Campus
cards.access_notes: Outdoor pedestrian route; allow extra time when campus is busy.

cards.title: Locate the student-union hub
cards.subtitle: Ackerman Union · beside Bruin Walk
cards.notes: Step inside to get familiar with the UCLA Store and restaurants, then use the building as a reliable reference point for later errands.
cards.short_summary: Identify the campus union and its everyday services.
cards.evidence_claim: UCLA’s self-guided tour lists Ackerman Union as a place to shop at the UCLA Store or get a meal.
cards.source_title: UCLA Self-Guided Walking Tour of Campus
cards.access_notes: Restaurant and store purchases are optional; check individual tenant access before visiting.

cards.title: See the Inverted Fountain
cards.subtitle: Ackerman Union area · observe the tradition
cards.notes: Find the fountain near Ackerman and learn the campus superstition; keep the stop to viewing rather than entering the water.
cards.short_summary: A quick campus-lore stop with a documented student superstition.
cards.evidence_claim: UCLA Admissions’ Bruin Blog documents the superstition that touching the Inverted Fountain before graduation means staying an extra quarter.
cards.access_notes: Observe from the surrounding plaza; do not enter the fountain or water.

cards.title: Climb Janss Steps
cards.subtitle: Janss Steps · original campus entrance
cards.notes: Take the steps at a comfortable pace and turn around at the top for the view across Wilson Plaza and the historic core.
cards.short_summary: A landmark climb connecting Wilson Plaza to the original campus core.
cards.evidence_claim: UCLA states that Janss Steps, originally called “the 87,” served as the university’s original entrance.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor stairway; use accessible campus routes if stairs are unsuitable.

cards.title: Pause at Royce Hall
cards.subtitle: Royce Quad · historic performing-arts building
cards.notes: Walk around the exterior and check the posted calendar if you want to return for a public concert, dance, or theater event.
cards.short_summary: See one of UCLA’s original buildings and its principal performing-arts auditorium.
cards.evidence_claim: UCLA describes Royce Hall as one of its four original buildings and says its 1,800-seat auditorium is the university’s main performing arts facility.
cards.access_notes: Exterior viewing is generally straightforward; event attendance and interior access depend on the program.

cards.title: Set up a future study stop
cards.subtitle: Powell Library · Dickson Plaza
cards.notes: Walk through the public library areas, note the study options, and save the library page for current hours and room information.
cards.short_summary: Familiarize yourself with UCLA’s main undergraduate library and study resources.
cards.evidence_claim: UCLA Library lists quiet and collaborative study spaces, group study rooms, computer access, and research help at Powell Library.
cards.access_notes: Hours vary; Night Powell is limited to current UCLA students, faculty, and staff with a physical BruinCard.

cards.title: Take an art-and-air break
cards.subtitle: Franklin D. Murphy Sculpture Garden · north campus
cards.notes: Follow the paths through the outdoor collection and choose one sculpture to revisit later, keeping clear of works and landscaped areas.
cards.short_summary: Explore UCLA’s outdoor sculpture collection between indoor stops.
cards.evidence_claim: The Fowler Museum describes the Franklin D. Murphy Sculpture Garden as spanning more than five acres and containing more than 70 sculptures.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor museum setting; respect barriers, artworks, and any site signage.

cards.title: Slow down in the garden
cards.subtitle: 707 Tiverton Drive · UCLA campus
cards.notes: Use the paths and interpretive signs for a quieter afternoon loop; stay on trails and leave plants and wildlife undisturbed.
cards.short_summary: A seven-day campus garden visit with seasonal posted hours.
cards.evidence_claim: The garden’s official page says it is open weekends 9 a.m.–5 p.m. from February through October and 9 a.m.–4 p.m. from November through January.
cards.access_notes: Check seasonal hours before leaving; posted closures include Thanksgiving and Christmas Day.

cards.title: Finish with open recreation
cards.subtitle: Sunset Canyon Recreation Center · Mapes Beach
cards.notes: If you have the needed recreation access and equipment, check the current schedule and use a court only during open-recreation availability.
cards.short_summary: Close the loop at UCLA’s sand volleyball courts.
cards.evidence_claim: UCLA Recreation says Mapes Beach has three regulation sand courts and one practice court, with open-recreation use first come, first served.
cards.access_notes: Open-recreation hours can vary with reservations or events; UCLA Recreation says participants must bring their own equipment.
